newsitem.title: FRANCE: French consultant sees CAC-40 objective of 2,650.
newsitem.headline: French consultant sees CAC-40 objective of 2,650.

text.p: French market research firm Jacques Chahine Finance has set an objective for the blue-chip CAC-40 index of 2,650 points assuming a very cautious scenario of 1.7 percent growth of French gross domestic product for 1997.
The forecast also assumes interest rates of 5.5 percent.
Assuming two percent growth, which is still below most market forecasts, the CAC-40 index could reach 2,900 to 3,000 by year's end, and 2,800 in the medium term, it said in a study.
The CAC closed at 2,634.48 points on Monday.
"The French market is the one showing the greatest recovery among European countries," it said.
"Even if price-earnings ratio seem high...at 18.6 times 1997 (earnings) for the CAC-40, this figure does not seem excessive in relation to very low interest rates under 5.5 percent," it said.
It said it expected French blue-chip results to outpace those of other European firms, with 20 percent profit growth seen in continental Europe and 22.7 percent growth for the CAC-40 companies.
It estimated estimated earnings of the CAC-40 would rebound 130 percent in 1996 from depressed 1995 levels. (( -- Paris Newsroom, +33 1 4221 5452 ))
